findings.title: Jeremiah 31:37: attributed quotation differs
findings.explanation: The Introduction attributes etnahta to the Aleppo ketiv; the note's explicit Aleppo quotation instead has U+05BD at that position. The note's MAM target has etnahta. Both sources agree that the gap for the qere lacks pointing. This establishes a disagreement between attributed quotations; it does not decide the manuscript reading. U+05BD occurs mid-verse, so it must not be described as silluq. The holam difference is a separate policy question. The chapter note revision 3088451 is newer than Introduction chapter 5 revision 3087740. Issue #304 is closed and concerned the formerly omitted atom only. The inspected revision already restores that atom; this audit does not reopen that correction.

findings.title: Deuteronomy roster: nine declared, eleven listed
findings.explanation: The header says nine items, but the roster contains eleven verse entries and twelve atom forms, because 32:10 supplies two. Notes support all eleven listed verse cases. Leningrad supplies the first six entries and Aleppo the last five. The manuscript readings agree; the count is stale. This does not prove that the roster is exhaustive.

findings.title: Lamentations 1:6: one and two are reversed
findings.explanation: The example calls the two-atom ketiv one atom and the one-atom qere two atoms. The section's own definition, visible forms, and parsed special ketiv/qere type agree on the opposite description. This verse has no doc-note; the corroboration is the parsed structure, not note silence.

findings.title: Proverbs 30:19: MAM illustration lacks the retained maqaf
findings.explanation: The Introduction's displayed MAM target has a space between the two atoms. The current note target has maqaf and explicitly agrees with Aleppo. The Introduction's own Aleppo quotation and maqaf policy agree with the note. The discrepancy belongs to the edition illustration; no competing Aleppo reading is established.

findings.title: Psalm 108:11: the quoted accent differs
findings.explanation: The Introduction quotation has U+0596 TIPEHA; the note has U+05AD DEHI in both its selected reading and the alternative attributed to Breuer. The nun-dagesh uncertainty agrees. The raw cache independently confirms the note quotation. This is an attributed-form disagreement, not a manuscript verdict.

findings.title: Psalms 57:9 and 108:3: secondary candidate accents differ
findings.explanation: Both sources prefer dehi with meteg. The Introduction secondary option is dehi with merkha; the notes instead propose terha with merkha. The difference appears in both the quoted codepoints and the explicit accent names. These are uncertain Aleppo candidate readings. The caches establish differing candidate sets; they do not select the actual manuscript reading.

findings.title: Current template catalogues differ from older category lists
findings.explanation: Chapter 2 lists three changed-qere cases; the appendix and current MAM structures have four, adding 2 Samuel 8:3. The appendix also lists nine two-atom annotation units while current MAM has eight, assigning 2 Samuel 21:12 to one three-atom unit. Nineteen catalogue memberships were checked: fifteen agree and four differ. This is catalogue drift under current MAM template identity. Traditional Masorah counts depend on manuscript and scope: at 8:3 the note expressly treats the extra qere atom differently in Aleppo and other manuscripts.

findings.title: Named marks and letters disagree while quoted forms agree
findings.explanation: At Exodus 7:20 the Introduction names merkha where its specimen and the note have TEVIR. At Numbers 16:27 it places segol on qof while the specimen and note place it on resh. At Numbers 22:23 it names bet instead of the note's dalet; the specimen has no bet. At Deuteronomy 28:27 the direction reverses: the Introduction names tet correctly, while the note calls that letter tav in its final clause. The quoted qere has tet and no tav. These are description discrepancies, not new manuscript readings. The uncertainty qualifier at Numbers 22:23 requires separate attention.

findings.title: Daniel 2:17: meteg differs in the Leningrad quotation
findings.explanation: The explicitly Leningrad-attributed Introduction specimen includes U+05BD under dalet; the note specimen omits it. Both describe the missing yod dagesh, and that phenomenon agrees. The extra meteg is a supported difference between the attributed quotations. Raw and parsed note captures agree. No notation-policy limitation was found in this local context, and the manuscript reading remains unverified.

findings.title: Daniel 5:7: yod differs in the Leningrad ketiv quotation
findings.explanation: The Introduction's explicitly Leningrad-attributed ketiv includes a yod after nun; the note's Leningrad ketiv omits that yod. The raw note agrees with the parsed note, and direct codepoint checks establish the consonantal difference. This is a supported source-quoted spelling discrepancy, with the manuscript reading still unverified.

findings.title: Daniel 7:9: the starred edition reading is reversed
findings.explanation: The decision list places the edition-selection star on the Leningrad full-first-yod form. The main spelling row and current MAM target select the defective-first-yod form instead. The note explicitly distinguishes these source spellings. This is an internal Introduction selection reversal corroborated by current edition evidence; the Leningrad manuscript claim itself agrees.

tracked.title: 2 Kings 18:27: shin dot
tracked.explanation: The Introduction's ketiv quotation has U+05C1; the quoted doc-note form omits it. The current issue comments attribute the decisive manuscript reading to Ben. No scan was consulted in this audit.

tracked.title: Ezekiel 28:3: meteg
tracked.explanation: The Introduction has U+05BD under dalet; the explicitly Aleppo-attributed note quotation omits it. The current issue comments attribute the decisive manuscript reading to Ben.

tracked.title: Ezekiel 14:14 and 14:20: nun's dagesh
tracked.explanation: Both Introduction quotations lack U+05BC on nun; both doc-note quotations include it and their prose explicitly describes nun as dageshed. Current issue comments attribute the manuscript readings to Ben.

uncertainty.title: 2 Samuel 21:12: scope of a single qere note
uncertainty.explanation: The chapter entry speaks of one qere note for two atoms; the note and appendix describe three. The chapter may describe only a subset. Cached evidence does not decide whether this is stale wording or deliberately partial scope.

uncertainty.title: Summary and chapter 2 disagree about doubled tsinnor visibility
uncertainty.explanation: The older Summary says the three listed phonetic features are not yet visible on Wikisource; chapter 2 says doubled tsinnor already appears. Current cached code contains the corresponding helper. No live template or browser rendering was examined, so actual current visibility remains unverified.

uncertainty.title: Psalm 66:12 and 119:90: membership in the maqaf list
uncertainty.explanation: The heading describes servant atoms with maqaf in Aleppo and MAM, but these quoted examples have a space; current text also has a space and no local note on this boundary. The list may have broadened to post-stress-meteg examples. Note silence cannot establish what Aleppo has.

uncertainty.title: Manuscript attribution remains incomplete
uncertainty.explanation: The cached notes corroborate some prose or gap claims without an explicitly named Aleppo manuscript or a complete corresponding ketiv quotation. Preserve this evidence as partial. A bare phrase meaning 'in the manuscript' is not an Aleppo sigil.

uncertainty.title: Genesis 36:13: shared accent-name wording anomaly
uncertainty.explanation: Both sources show U+05A3 twice while both call the accent merkha. U+05A3's Unicode name is MUNAH. The sources agree with each other, so this is not an Introduction/doc-note contradiction. No manuscript interpretation is changed.

uncertainty.title: Psalm 1:3: added grey maqaf absent from the illustration
uncertainty.explanation: The current parsed text has the added grey maqaf, as the Introduction policy describes; the displayed example lacks it. No local doc-note addresses that boundary. Keep this separate from the note-supported Proverbs illustration finding.

uncertainty.title: Malachi 2:7: incidental holam in the specimen
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction specimen includes holam; the explicit Aleppo note quotation omits it and quotes an absence explanation. The meteg claim agrees. The specimen may follow a different convention for conventional divine-name pointing; assess that scope before treating the incidental mark as a manuscript contradiction.

uncertainty.title: Psalm 119:138: incidental meteg without an explicit Introduction sigil
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction specimen adds meteg on initial vav; the note specimen lacks it. Both address the extra revia. The Introduction row lacks an explicit manuscript sigil, so do not invent Aleppo attribution for the incidental meteg.

uncertainty.title: Psalm 18:2: Aleppo attribution inside the declared missing range
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction uses an explicit Aleppo sigil for this form, although its missing-extent roster covers Psalms 15:1 through 25:1. The note discusses other named manuscripts and reading tradition. An unquoted prior report or shorthand could account for the attribution; the caches do not supply it. The grammatical claim agrees, so this is an attribution question, not proof of a false manuscript reading.

uncertainty.title: Leningrad candidate attribution and digital-transcription qualifiers
uncertainty.explanation: Several Introduction entries place disputed candidates under Leningrad while the current notes attribute some candidates to other manuscripts or only to the digital transcription, or retain a digital-transcription qualifier absent from the Introduction. The batch ledgers retain exact source units. These are attribution-precision questions; the caches do not settle the physical reading.

uncertainty.title: Deuteronomy 5:13: reading-strand assignments exceed the note
uncertainty.explanation: The Introduction assigns the two quoted marks to reading strands more specifically than the note's explicit Leningrad description of munah and merkha. The quoted marks themselves are corroborated. Keep the strand assignment as a separate source-scope question.

uncertainty.title: Shared or incidental explanation differences
uncertainty.explanation: Song of Songs 4:16 names lamed, although the difference between the displayed MAM and Leningrad specimens is dagesh on zayin; lamed is undotted in both. At Lamentations 4:7 both specimens encode segol on shin while the descriptions discuss qamats and the note preserves uncertainty about close dots. These are explanation questions, not independent disagreements about the manuscript reading.

controls.title: Proverbs 30:5: Aleppo's omitted revia dot agrees
controls.explanation: Both sources attribute the omitted revia dot to Aleppo. Ordering of the Introduction's displayed accents differs from MAM's order; that literal encoding difference is not a competing manuscript reading.

controls.title: Job 11:6: oleh position agrees
controls.explanation: Both sources attribute the same oleh position to Aleppo. The printed alternative is explicitly distinguished. Source strings retain their original mark order.
